name: 1628 Prairie Avenue — brick house, the south half of the pair with 1626, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D), the south half of the pair with 1626'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: T-2355 (piece 1 of T-1862) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id: the main body is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — K03 brick on all four walls, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop, K09 window heads, K10 bracketed cornice, a K04/K05 hip — instead of the draft builder, as T-2353 built 1616. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (storeys '3B', brick, the south half of a pair attached to 1626, the traced main body) through the T-1840 census. Its north wall is the party wall it shares with 1626 and is built blank. Everything else is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1628-brick-front-2355. T-2391 stands the piece the sheet draws behind the north part of the rear wall on K01's rear wings (T-2343): the census row s20-1628-a1 reads it '1B brick rear piece', one storey over a basement, where the draft had drawn it three storeys by its own rule. No photograph, plate or description of 1628 has been read; a later reading that finds one replaces the kit's choices here.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1628 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1628 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 33.750, v -2.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.579 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle inside the traced main part of s20fp-1628-b1 (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s20.json, T-2328), kept from the draft (12.25 m deep, 6.0 m along the front; the part's two rectangles cover 90% of its fill). The trace also draws the rear piece behind the north part of the rear wall (the draft's r2, which it drew three storeys and 4.5 m out), which is rear_wings (T-2391).

stories.note: '3B; rear 1B' printed on the 1911 sheet: three full storeys over a basement. The rear 1B is the frame porch the trace draws at the front's south end, which the K07 stoop stands in. The '1B' behind it is the rear piece's (rear_wings).

construction.note: The register reads the map's colours as 'brick'. T-2355: built as a brick house, front and all — K01's `brick` construction (T-2341), the K03 common brick on every wall, with stone dressings on the street front.

principal_floor_m.note: The draft's raised principal floor over the basement the sheet's 'B' prints, inside the K01 contract's principal_floor range [0.8, 1.8]; it solves to whole risers of the K07 stoop (the brief's 'high stoop').

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, diminishing upward, as 1808's three storeys have them in the same kit; the draft drew 3.9, 3.5 and 3.3. No source reads this house's heights.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A 13-inch brick wall, inside the contract's masonry range [0.23, 0.45]; the sheet prints no wall thickness for this lot.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: Common brick, a 13-inch wall, as the front.

service_wall_brick.note: The sheet colours the house brick; the fabric, bond, heads, string course and grime are the K03 library's common buff brick in common bond (the one panel k03_brick lays), on all four walls since the street front is brick too. No photograph of 1628 has been read, so the brick's colour and bond are the kit's, not the house's.

street_front_trim.note: The street front's window heads: the K09 stone lintel under a cornice hood on the two lower storeys, as 1616 has them, and K01's flat stone lintel on the low third storey, as 1808's top storey; the door keeps K01's flat stone lintel. No source shows 1628's heads.

wall_head.note: A K10 bracketed timber cornice (data/components/prairie_1904/k10_cornices.json): scrolled brackets and bed moulding under the K05 soffit, round all four walls, as on 1608, 1612 and 1616 up the row. The draft drew 1628 unbracketed; no source reads its eave either way. No cresting: none is read.

roof_form.note: A hip roof, the one K01 builds (k01.roof.hip), low-pitched behind the bracketed eave, as the draft drew it. No source reads this roof; a three-storey pair of this period may as well have stood under flat roofs behind a cornice, which K01 cannot build yet (T-2350 asks for K05's flat roof).

roof_pitch_deg.note: Low, inside the contract's ordinary range [25, 45]: an Italianate hip over a full third storey, with no attic to light. 30 because, on this 12.25 x 6.0 m plan, it is a pair the K05 roof union this kit dresses its caps on parts cleanly (see docs/RESEARCH/k01-1628-brick-2355). Tinned rather than slated, because K04's Pennsylvania slate is cut for a 45 degree roof.

eave_overhang_m.note: A deep Italianate eave over the brackets; the fascia and soffit close it. 0.6 m is an eave the K05 union builds at this roof's pitch (see roof_pitch_deg).

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A landing one door-swing deep before the threshold.

stoop_width_m.note: The stoop half again the door's width.

entrance_bay.note: The door on the south half of the 6.0 m front, mirrored from 1626's north door so the pair's doors stand at their outer ends (the draft rules' row frontage-20-008, entrance south); the trace's frame porch (s20fp-1628-b1 p1) stands there too. No source reads which half.

front_bays.note: Two bays across the 6.0 m front, south to north: the door and the windows over it on the south, a window a storey on the north against the party wall. The draft drew two.

side_bays.note: Three windows a storey along the south wall, rear to front, one to each room of a three-room-deep house; the wall faces 1630's side yard. The north wall is the party wall with 1626 and is blank, as K01 builds it.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall, north to south. The northern one (s 1.0 m) stands where the rear piece joins (rear_wings, T-2391): on the principal storey it is behind the piece and is not cut, the opening into it; on the two upper storeys, above the piece's deck, it is a window. The southern one moved from s 4.1 to s 5.1 with T-2391: at 4.1 its head straddled the piece's south wall (s 4.05), which K01 refuses, so it now stands in the 1.95 m of rear wall south of the piece, 0.9 m in from the south corner as the northern one is 1.0 m in from the north.

rear_wings.note: T-2391: the piece the 1911 sheet draws behind the north part of the rear wall, whose PLACE and storey count are read from the map and whose form is K01's reconstruction. Read on sheet 20 (T-1840 census s20-1628-a1, '1B brick rear piece'; trace s20fp-1628-b1 p2, the draft's r2) and measured off the raster through the T-1250 fit, in this frame: u -4.75 to 0 (the trace's outer wall at u -4.75 to -4.81 against the main rear wall's line at u 0) and v 1.95 to 6.0 (the trace's south wall at v 1.93-1.94; its north wall on the party line with 1626 at v 6.2, built flush with the main body's north wall at 6.0, since K01's wing stands inside its host wall). The sheet colours it brick and letters it '1B': one storey over a basement. The draft (T-2334) drew it three storeys, its rules' count for a wing inside the main part; the sheet's letter is followed. Its floor is the main body's principal floor (1.4 m) and its storey the main body's first (4.0 m), so its deck, at 5.7 m, stands under the main body's second-storey sills. K06 sash, two in its south wall over 1630's side yard and one in its rear wall, and the flat painted-tin deck on a 0.3 m fascia with a 0.15 m overhang: all reconstructed, as 1604's, 1616's and 1634's wings. The north wall is blank: it is the party wall with 1626's own rear piece, which the sheet draws against it and lettered the same '1B'. The dot the sheet prints in the piece's south-west corner is not modelled.

sash_by_storey.note: Double-hung sash, diminishing upward, inside the contract's sash ranges, as 1808's three storeys.

basement_lights.note: Area lights in the front wall, the basement the sheet's 'B' records.

roof_covering.note: Painted tin in standing seams, K04's cover for a roof too low for its slate, with copper ridge and hip rolls and copper flashings. No source reads 1616's roof.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks on the ridge over spine walls between the front, middle and back rooms, as 1608's, 1612's and 1616's; the draft drew two. No source reads this house's chimneys.

rainwater.note: K04's half-round copper gutter round the eave and round copper downpipes to splash stones: one at the front's north corner by the party wall (the south half carries the stoop), one on the south wall between its windows, two on the rear wall: one at its south corner and one just south of the rear piece (T-2391 moved it off the north corner the piece now stands against). The piece's deck has no gutter, as 1604's, 1616's and 1634's wings'. K01 stands no pipe on its north wall. All reconstructed.

window_kit.note: Every window from the K06 kit: two-over-two double-hung sash, the kit's commonest form, not a reading of this house; the basement lights the kit's area light.

entrance_kit.note: The K07 kit's four-panel door under a two-light transom at the head of a straight stone stoop solved from the principal floor. front_yard_m is the street grid's own distance: the draft's front stands 9.38 m behind the Prairie Avenue street line (street_u 21.633 less the 12.25 m body) and the walk begins 1 ft further out (row_66 margin band), 9.69 m.

boundary.note: T-3216: no picture of this front is held, so the boundary is a STATED RECONSTRUCTION on the west side of the block's pictured fronts, every one of which closes its street line and gates its walk: 1612's photograph (an iron spear fence on its curb, a pair of entrance gates at the stoop's foot and a gate across the south passage), 1620's 1874 engraving and 1898 sketch (an iron lattice on its base with gate piers at the walk), 1616's boarded street line in the same 1874 plate, and 1638's photograph (iron bars on a stone base between gate piers). Built as the K11 kit's spear fence on its curb, the plainest of them and the block's photographed iron, with the kit's pair of entrance leaves on stone piers, 1.3 m clear on the stoop's centre, standing open (drawn 70 degrees) as 1612's photograph and both pictures of 1620 show their entrance gates. No side gate: the house stands 0.71 m from its south lot line, less than the kit's gate needs between a pier and the wall (0.9 m clear past a 0.5 m pier), so there is no passage to gate and the iron runs unbroken from the lot line to the entrance (K11's T-3216 rule). The street line is parcel prairie_1628's street corners (data/street_grid/1904.json) carried into this frame, 9.375 m before the front. The lot's sides are the same parcel's, s -0.71 and 6.21. RECONSTRUCTED: the fence's kind, height and line, its gates and their set; liberty L-k11-fences-1600-block-3216.

yard.note: T-3216 (the owner, 2026-10-27: every worked house's walk to its door, its gates and its boundaries to their pictures; where no picture shows them, a stated reconstruction consistent with the block). No picture of 1628's front is held. The walk is laid on the block's pictured fronts (1612's photograph shows a light paved walk from the public walk through its open entrance gateway to the stoop's foot, and 1616's and 1621's walks are built on it): flags from the stoop's foot through the entrance gate, the gate's width, to the inner edge of the public walk; the lawn covers the rest of the front yard inside the iron. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's line, flags, width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; no service walk is built (no picture shows a side passage's floor); liberty L-k14-walks-1600-block-3216.
